title: Best Walking Socks UK
short: Merino and synthetic walking and hiking socks compared by season, cushioning and fit, including women's versions.
intro: The right walking sock keeps your feet dry, cushioned and blister-free, whether you are on a local footpath or a multi-day trek. This guide compares socks tested by UK outdoor publications, and notes which have a women's version.

guide.q: Merino wool or synthetic walking socks?
guide.a: Merino is soft, controls odour and regulates temperature well. Synthetic socks dry faster and often cost less. Many of the best socks blend both.

guide.q: What thickness of walking sock do I need?
guide.a: Lightweight socks suit summer and low-cut shoes. Midweight socks suit most three-season walking. Heavyweight socks suit winter and boots, but can be too warm in hot weather.

guide.q: Do women need women's-specific walking socks?
guide.a: Some brands offer women's versions with a narrower or shorter fit. They are worth trying if unisex socks slip or bunch, and we note where a women's version is available.

guide.q: How do I stop blisters when walking?
guide.a: Choose a snug sock that does not bunch, avoid cotton, which holds sweat, and make sure your boots fit. Double-layer socks can also reduce friction.
